text:
What it takes from me in fire, the hand hiding your eyes gives me in snow; the whiteness that kills is no less cruel and stirs no lesser flames.


Sight drinks the fires fresh and spreads them like a volcano through the veins; the loving breast regards that whiteness fearfully, feeling it treacherous.


If you pass your hand across the tyrant ardor of your eyes to temper it, that is great pity for a human heart.


But not for you: though snow, your hand may melt when hiding it, unless your hand instead intends to freeze it.

translation.title: To Aminta, Who Covered Her Eyes with Her Hand
